ms.mechanism: Chemotherapeutic agent that intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II, causing DNA strand breaks and cell death. Broad immunosuppression including B cells, T cells, and macrophages.
ms.approval: FDA approved 2000 (worsening RMS, SPMS). Last-line therapy due to cardiotoxicity and leukemia risk. Strict 140 mg/m² lifetime cumulative dose limit.

ms.mechanism: High-dose IV corticosteroid for acute MS relapses. Rapidly reduces inflammation, restores BBB integrity, accelerates relapse recovery. No effect on long-term disease course or disability progression.
ms.approval: Standard of care for acute MS relapses. Not a disease-modifying therapy.

ra.mechanism: Soluble TNFR2-Fc fusion protein that acts as a decoy receptor, neutralizing both TNF-alpha and lymphotoxin-alpha
ra.approval: FDA approved 1998 (RA). First approved anti-TNF biologic.

ra.mechanism: PEGylated humanized anti-TNF Fab fragment (no Fc region); neutralizes TNF without inducing complement or ADCC cytotoxicity
ra.approval: FDA approved 2009 (RA). Can be used in pregnancy (minimal placental transfer).

ra.mechanism: Humanized anti-IL-6R monoclonal antibody blocking both membrane-bound and soluble IL-6R, inhibiting IL-6-mediated JAK1/JAK2-STAT3 signaling
ra.approval: FDA approved 2010 (RA). Superior to adalimumab in monotherapy (ADACTA trial).

ssc.mechanism: Humanized anti-IL-6R monoclonal antibody blocking both membrane-bound and soluble IL-6R, inhibiting IL-6-mediated JAK1/JAK2-STAT3 signaling and reducing inflammation and fibrosis
ssc.approval: FDA approved 2021 for SSc-ILD (focuSSced trial). First biologic approved for SSc.

ra.mechanism: Fully human anti-IL-6Rα monoclonal antibody; higher affinity for IL-6R than tocilizumab
ra.approval: FDA approved 2017 (RA). Fully human antibody reduces immunogenicity risk.

ra.mechanism: Oral selective JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor; blocks signaling downstream of IL-6, type I IFN, IFN-gamma, and GM-CSF receptors
ra.approval: FDA approved 2018 (RA). Superior to adalimumab in RA-BEAM trial.

sle.mechanism: JAK1/2 inhibitor blocking type I IFN, IL-6, and other cytokine signaling
sle.approval: Phase 3 trials in SLE (SLE-BRAVE I & II); mixed results

ss.mechanism: JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor blocking type I IFN, IL-6, and other cytokine signaling
ss.approval: Phase 2 in SS being explored

ra.mechanism: CTLA4-Ig fusion protein that binds CD80/CD86 on APCs, blocking CD28-mediated T cell costimulation and reducing T cell activation
ra.approval: FDA approved 2005 (RA). Only approved T cell costimulation blocker.

ss.mechanism: CTLA4-Ig fusion protein blocking CD28-mediated T cell costimulation; reduces Tfh cell help to B cells
ss.approval: FDA approved for RA. Phase 3 in SS (ASAP-III) showed mixed results but ongoing investigation.

t1d.mechanism: CTLA4-Ig fusion protein that binds CD80/CD86 on antigen-presenting cells, blocking CD28-mediated T cell costimulation and reducing islet-reactive T cell activation and expansion
t1d.category: Investigational Biologic - T Cell Costimulation Blocker
t1d.approval: Investigational for T1D. Phase 2 trial showed 9.6-month delay in C-peptide decline. FDA approved for RA but not T1D.

ra.mechanism: Inhibits endosomal acidification, blocking TLR7/9 activation; reduces antigen presentation and cytokine production
ra.approval: FDA approved 1955. Mild DMARD used in combination therapy for mild-moderate RA.

sle.mechanism: Inhibits endosomal acidification, blocking TLR7/9 activation and reducing type I IFN production
sle.approval: Standard of care for all SLE patients

ss.mechanism: Inhibits endosomal acidification, blocking TLR7/9-mediated pDC activation and IFN-α production. Reduces immune complex-mediated inflammation.
ss.approval: Off-label first-line for SS (not FDA-approved for SS). Standard of care in clinical practice. Guidelines recommend for inflammatory musculoskeletal symptoms.

ra.mechanism: Inhibits de novo pyrimidine synthesis by blocking DHODH, selectively reducing activated T lymphocyte proliferation
ra.approval: FDA approved 1998 (RA). Alternative first-line DMARD to methotrexate.

ss.mechanism: Inhibits DHODH, blocking de novo pyrimidine synthesis → selectively reduces activated lymphocyte proliferation
ss.approval: Off-label for SS inflammatory arthritis. Used as alternative to hydroxychloroquine or MTX for articular symptoms.

ra.mechanism: Prodrug cleaved by gut bacteria into 5-ASA and sulfapyridine; inhibits NF-κB, reduces inflammatory cytokine production, and scavenges reactive oxygen species
ra.approval: FDA approved 1950. Part of triple therapy (MTX+SSZ+HCQ).

ra.mechanism: Recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra); competitively blocks IL-1α and IL-1β binding to IL-1R1
ra.approval: FDA approved 2001 (RA). Limited use due to daily injections and modest efficacy vs TNF inhibitors.

ra.mechanism: Fully human anti-RANKL monoclonal antibody; inhibits osteoclast differentiation and activation by blocking RANK-RANKL interaction
ra.approval: FDA approved 2010 (osteoporosis). Used in RA to prevent bone erosion and glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis.

ra.mechanism: Inhibits de novo purine synthesis, selectively suppressing T and B lymphocyte proliferation
ra.approval: Used off-label for refractory RA and RA-ILD (interstitial lung disease). Limited efficacy data.

sle.mechanism: Inhibits de novo purine synthesis, selectively suppressing lymphocyte proliferation
sle.approval: Widely used off-label for lupus nephritis; standard of care

ss.mechanism: Inhibits IMPDH, blocking de novo purine synthesis → suppresses T and B lymphocyte proliferation
ss.approval: Off-label for severe systemic SS (interstitial lung disease, nephritis, CNS). Used as steroid-sparing agent.

ssc.mechanism: Inhibits de novo purine synthesis, selectively suppressing T and B lymphocyte proliferation; reduces inflammatory cell infiltration in skin and lung
ssc.approval: Standard of care for SSc-ILD (SLS II trial). First-line immunosuppressant for SSc. Off-label.

ra.mechanism: Oral selective JAK1 inhibitor with 30-fold selectivity over JAK2; blocks IL-6, type I/II IFN, and common gamma chain cytokine signaling
ra.approval: Approved in EU/Japan 2020 (RA). Not FDA approved (pending). JAK1 selectivity profile.

ra.mechanism: Bispecific anti-TNF/anti-HSA nanobody (VHH); engineered for extended half-life via albumin binding and enhanced tissue penetration due to small size (38 kDa vs 150 kDa IgG)

sle.mechanism: Binds and neutralizes soluble BAFF, reducing B cell survival and autoantibody production

ssc.approval: FDA approved for SLE and lupus nephritis. Investigational in SSc: Phase 2 trial and case series suggest benefit. Off-label use in refractory SSc.

sle.approval: FDA approved 2021 (moderate to severe SLE)

sle.mechanism: Calcineurin inhibitor; blocks T cell activation and podocyte stabilization in the kidney
sle.approval: FDA approved 2021 (lupus nephritis)

sle.approval: Reserved for severe organ-threatening lupus (nephritis, CNS, pulmonary)

ssc.mechanism: Alkylating agent that crosslinks DNA, inhibiting lymphocyte proliferation; immunosuppressive effect via depletion of activated T and B cells
ssc.approval: SLS I trial demonstrated efficacy in SSc-ILD. Used for severe/progressive SSc-ILD and scleroderma renal crisis. IV or oral.

sle.mechanism: Type II anti-CD20 antibody with enhanced B cell depletion vs rituximab
sle.approval: Phase 3 in lupus nephritis (REGENCY trial, positive results 2024)

sle.mechanism: Highly selective, irreversible second-generation BTK inhibitor with reduced off-target kinase inhibition vs ibrutinib

sle.mechanism: Selective C5a receptor antagonist that blocks C5a-mediated neutrophil activation, migration, and adhesion

sle.mechanism: Blocks CD40-CD40L interaction, preventing T cell-dependent B cell activation and germinal center formation

sle.mechanism: Long-acting monoclonal antibody that binds C5 and blocks cleavage into C5a and C5b-9 (MAC)

sle.approval: Phase 3 in SLE (PHOENYCS GO trial, ongoing)

ss.approval: FDA approved 1994 for radiation-induced xerostomia; used off-label for SS sicca. Symptomatic therapy only.

ss.mechanism: Selective M1/M3 muscarinic agonist with longer half-life and potentially fewer side effects than pilocarpine

ssc.approval: FDA approved 2019 for SSc-associated ILD (SENSCIS trial). Also approved for IPF.

ssc.mechanism: Dual endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) blocking both ETA and ETB receptors; reduces pulmonary vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, and fibrosis driven by endothelin-1
ssc.approval: FDA approved for SSc-PAH (WHO Group 1). First oral ERA for PAH. Also prevents new digital ulcers in SSc.

ssc.mechanism: Selective ETA receptor antagonist with high affinity; blocks endothelin-1 mediated vasoconstriction and vascular smooth muscle proliferation in the pulmonary vasculature
ssc.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). Selective ETA blocking spares ETB-mediated vasodilation and endothelin clearance.

ssc.mechanism: Dual ERA with enhanced tissue penetration and sustained receptor binding; blocks endothelin-1 induced vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, and fibrosis
ssc.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). SERAPHIN trial. Improved tissue targeting vs bosentan.

ssc.mechanism: Selective PDE5 inhibitor preventing cGMP degradation; enhances nitric oxide-mediated vasodilation in the pulmonary vasculature
ssc.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). First-line and add-on therapy. Short-acting PDE5i.

ssc.mechanism: Long-acting selective PDE5 inhibitor; once-daily dosing with sustained pulmonary vasodilation via NO-cGMP pathway enhancement
ssc.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). Once-daily dosing convenience. Preferred long-acting PDE5i.

ssc.mechanism: Synthetic prostacyclin analogue activating IP receptor; induces potent pulmonary and systemic vasodilation, inhibits platelet aggregation, and suppresses smooth muscle proliferation
ssc.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). Multiple formulations: IV, SC (Remodulin), inhaled (Tyvaso), oral (Orenitram).

ssc.mechanism: Oral selective IP receptor agonist (non-prostanoid); prodrug metabolized to ACT-333679, which activates IP receptor on vascular smooth muscle, causing vasodilation
ssc.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). GRIPHON trial. First oral IP receptor agonist; more convenient than prostacyclin infusions.

ssc.mechanism: Selective CB2 receptor agonist that activates resolution of innate immune responses; reduces pro-fibrotic cytokine production (TGF-β, IL-6) and promotes anti-inflammatory lipid mediator production
ssc.approval: Investigational. Phase 2 RESOLVE-1 trial in dcSSc showed promise; Phase 3 did not meet primary endpoint for mRSS. Not yet approved.

ssc.mechanism: Fully human pan-TGF-β neutralizing monoclonal antibody; blocks all three TGF-β isoforms, inhibiting fibroblast activation, myofibroblast differentiation, and ECM deposition
ssc.approval: Investigational for SSc. Phase 1 trial showed target engagement and TGF-β pathway suppression in SSc skin. Not yet approved.

ssc.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH, PATENT-1 trial) and CTEPH. Unique dual mechanism (NO-dependent and NO-independent).
